## Travel, passage and distance

**Distance and travel** (decided 19 October 2026, build order item 7). Everything travels the map physically, by one measure of distance, so journeys differ greatly in length and in how likely they are to arrive. Each connection has a length weighted by its terrain, so travel time follows real distance rather than equal steps between provinces (decided 21 October 2026; "Map review").

**Passage and access** (decided in part; build order items 7 and 9). Whether envoys, gold and armies may cross foreign territory, what the host may do when they pass, and whether sealed tablets can grant passage, basing or trade rights, including for allies marching on a common enemy. Passage, basing and trade rights granted on sealed tablets come with envoy authority (item 9). Decided 19 October 2026: a host can stop anyone passing through his land, and what he does with them is his choice. A traveller who passes openly can be stopped at will; one who sneaks through is found only if a chance check discovers him, and the odds weigh his skills and what he carries against what the host spends on policing in that province. The check is part of interception on the road (item 7).

**Distance inside your own realm** (decided 19 October 2026: the same time restrictions apply inside a realm as between courts; built with "Command at a distance", build order item 13). Today a king sees and commands his whole realm instantly. Instead, news from provinces and orders to armies travel to and from the capital, as when the pharaoh learned of the Levant weeks late. This weakens the size advantage, makes scheduled orders essential, and lets the map show the last known state of distant provinces with its date. Gold reaches the treasury after its travel time ("One treasury, many stores"). Roads and relay stations with upkeep (build order item 15), in the spirit of Egypt's fortified Ways of Horus across Sinai, speed messages and orders but also invading armies, can be captured or cut, and can be built jointly with a neighbor under a sealed tablet, though messages passing through a neighbor's stations may be read there. Every order a king gives inside his realm travels from where he is, levies included: a levy at the far end of the realm is raised when the order gets there, not in the season it is given, unless a governor there raises it under his own mandate ("Governors" under "Command at a distance"). This is what gives moving the capital its point despite the risk, and what makes roads, relay stations and policing worth paying for. Orders and reports inside the realm travel with the realm's own couriers (decided 21 October 2026): men in a unit, like caravans, not named characters, since they speak the realm's own language and need no audience at a foreign court. In hostile land they can be stopped, and a captured order can be read by whoever has a reader. A letter to a foreign court still needs a character ("No faceless channel"). What a king sees as current is whatever a courier could bring him within the season, and everything else shows its last report with its date. No circle is computed: his reach grows with roads, relay stations and river boats, shrinks in winter, when the passes lie under snow, and moves with him, and the map can draw it around him as a display.
